name: Fighter Dragon Lancer
body:
Powerful spearmen who are known to rival the dragon for mastery of the skies with their sheer martial prowess.

Offensive Focus

A dragon lancer is not proficient in heavy armor or tower shields. This modifies weapon and armor proficiencies.

Jump (Ex)

At 1st level, a dragon lancer can add their Strength bonus on Acrobatics checks instead of their Dexterity modifier and their high jumps are treated as long jumps when determining the DC. When the dragon lancer jumps they can momentarily hang midair; they do not fall until the end of their turn, allowing them to attack or perform other actions midair. If the dragon lancer grapples a creature capable of bearing their weight, instead of falling they can remain adjacent to the creature as it moves. This replaces the bonus feat gained at 1st level.

Dragon-Hearted (Ex)

A dragon lancer doubles their bonus to fear from bravery against creatures with the dragon type. This modifies bravery.

Dragon Thrust (Ex)

At 3rd level, a dragon lancer learns to wield the skies as effectively as their mortal foes. They gain Branch Pounce as a bonus feat and as a full round action, a dragon lancer can make an Acrobatics check to jump before making a charge, which can trigger the Branch Pounce feat effect. When using Acrobatics in this way, dragon lancers are always counted as having a running start. This signature technique allows them to easily reposition around threats and obstacles, or use their extra momentum down on their enemies. Additionally, when using Acrobatics, the dragon lancer ignores fall damage equal to the height they successfully jumped.

This replaces armor training 1 and armor mastery.

Spear Specialty (Ex)

A dragon lancer must select Spears or Polearms with their weapon training.

Acrobatic Prowess (Ex)

At 7th level, a dragon lancer’s jumping skills continue to improve. They add their level on all Acrobatics checks, and high jumps are no longer limited by their movement. Additionally, when a dragon lancer willingly falls, they take all falling damage as nonlethal and are never made prone after falling or missing a Branch Pounce attack. This replaces armor training 2.

Winged Glide (Ex)

At 11th level, when jumping a dragon lancer can choose not to fall until the end of their next turn instead.

This cannot be used in simultaneous turns until 15th level. At that point, they can maintain this ability for an additional simultaneous turn. This replaces armor training 3 and 4.
